stories.title: Faculty Senate passes vote of no confidence in UMPD and University’s handling of GEO negotiations
stories.summary: The University of Michigan Faculty Senate passed a vote of no confidence in the University's handling of Graduate Employees' Organization (GEO) negotiations and the University of Michigan Police Department (UMPD). This vote was part of a broader motion expressing solidarity with GEO and pro-Palestine activists, and criticizing the administration's response to activism.

inputFacts.title: Faculty Senate passes vote of no confidence in UMPD and University’s handling of GEO negotiations
inputFacts.summary: The University of Michigan Faculty Senate has officially passed a vote of no confidence regarding the University of Michigan Police Department and the administration's management of negotiations with the Graduate Employees' Organization. The vote reflects growing faculty dissatisfaction with institutional leadership and campus safety policies.

stories.title: World premiere of oratorio 'Don't Let the Sun' at U-M
stories.summary: The University of Michigan will premiere "Don't Let the Sun," an oratorio exploring the history of "sundown towns" in the U.S., including their prevalence outside the South. The work, commissioned by U-M, aims to educate audiences on this hidden dimension of American history and encourage reflection on building welcoming communities.

inputFacts.title: World premiere of oratorio 'Don't Let the Sun' at U-M
inputFacts.summary: A new oratorio titled 'Don't Let the Sun' explores the history of sundown towns in America. Inspired by sociologist James Loewen, the work will be performed by the U-M Chamber Choir and University Choir at Hill Auditorium on November 17.

stories.title: Midterm voters ended the long-running GOP dominance in state legislatures
stories.summary: Midterm elections resulted in Democrats gaining control of state legislatures in several states, including Michigan, where they now hold a "trifecta" with the governorship. This shift could lead to policy changes on issues such as taxes, reproductive rights, healthcare access, and school funding.

inputFacts.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: The World of Ann Arbor's Fairy Doors
inputFacts.summary: Journalist Joshua Nieman explores the origins and cultural impact of the mysterious 'fairy doors' found throughout Ann Arbor. He interviews Jonathan B. Wright, a local fairyologist who explains how the artistic movement began in his own home and expanded into the city.

inputFacts.title: DTE to sell non-utility business to fund grid upgrades, data center growth
inputFacts.summary: DTE Energy plans to sell its non-utility subsidiary, DTE Vantage, for $3 billion to help finance infrastructure upgrades and support the expansion of data center capacity. The move comes as the utility faces scrutiny over rate hike requests and legal challenges regarding its data center contracts and environmental compliance at its EES Coke Battery facility.

inputFacts.title: City of Chelsea reviews hiring protocol as search for new city manager begins
inputFacts.summary: The city of Chelsea is implementing a new "relational recruiting" approach to hire a new city manager following the resignation of former manager Elle Cole. Mayor Kate Henson reports that the city is focusing on fostering a supportive work culture while also prioritizing infrastructure projects like water and wastewater treatment plant expansions.

inputFacts.title: McDonald’s giving away free turkeys at 12 Metro Detroit locations -- here’s where
inputFacts.summary: Twelve McDonald’s locations across Metro Detroit are partnering with local community organizations to distribute free turkeys on Thursday, November 19. The turkeys will be provided on a first-come, first-served basis while supplies last, with a limit of one per vehicle.

inputFacts.title: Ann Arbor wins best tasting water in Michigan award
inputFacts.summary: Ann Arbor has been awarded first place in the 2026 annual Michigan regional water-tasting competition. The city's public water supply was evaluated by the American Water Works Association's Best Tasting Water Committee.

inputFacts.title: ‘It will get better’: Former U.S. Sen. Jeff Flake advocates for bipartisan cooperation
inputFacts.summary: Former U.S. Senator Jeff Flake visited to discuss the importance of bipartisan cooperation in American politics. He expressed optimism about the future of the political climate.

inputFacts.title: Michigan attorney general-elect prepares to leave Washtenaw County prosecutor role
inputFacts.summary: Washtenaw County Prosecutor Eli Savit is stepping down from his position early next month. He is leaving the role to prepare for his upcoming term as Michigan's attorney general.

inputFacts.title: SACUA discusses research funding, support for branch campuses
inputFacts.summary: The University of Michigan’s Senate Advisory Committee on University Affairs met to address budgetary transparency, identity, and faculty rights regarding the university's branch campuses. The meeting was led by SACUA Vice Chair Kirsten Herold in the absence of Chair Kentaro Toyama.

inputFacts.title: Waypoint Outreach Initiative aims to support those dealing with reentry, homelessness, and other challenges
inputFacts.summary: The Ypsilanti-based Waypoint Outreach Initiative is a new volunteer organization focused on street outreach, peer support, and reentry services for women. The group is hosting a public workshop on November 21, 2026, at the Ypsilanti District Library to introduce their programming and connect community members with local resources.

inputFacts.title: Ypsi schools' Dr. Alena Zachery-Ross on being named state Superintendent of the Year
inputFacts.summary: Dr. Alena Zachery-Ross, superintendent of Ypsilanti Community Schools, discusses her recent recognition as Michigan Superintendent of the Year. She emphasizes the importance of community partnerships, student-centered leadership, and the collective strength of her district's educators and scholars.
